verdict.rationale: GitLab's own docs show it scans source code with SAST and scans dependencies, including runtime, development and transitive packages, as well as libraries and container images. That establishes the scanning capability, but the pack never lists which languages or package ecosystems are supported, so breadth across 'all major' ones is unproven. Missing for 10: a documented list of supported languages, a documented list of supported package managers/ecosystems, and independent or hands-on corroboration of coverage breadth.

support.subject: As a developer, I can scan projects across all the major languages and package ecosystems my organization uses

citations.quote: Application security testing scans your project’s source code, dependencies, libraries, and container images.
Dependency scanning identifies known security vulnerabilities in your project’s dependencies, including runtime, development, and transitive (nested) packages.
SAST scans happen automatically with each commit
